name: University of California, Davis
character: Set in the Sacramento Valley, the vast, bike-friendly campus centers on a large rectangular quad and features a 100-acre arboretum with 4,000 trees, Putah Creek, Lake Spafford, and buildings ranging from historic halls to an angular, metallic design.

landmarks.name: the Quad
landmarks.quote: Towards the northeast end of campus is the Quad, a large rectangular field, which was the historic geographic center of campus.
landmarks.look: Large rectangular open green field bordered by campus buildings.

landmarks.name: Peter J. Shields Library
landmarks.quote: The Peter J. Shields Library has three different architectural styles due to various construction and extensions being added
landmarks.look: Large library building combining three distinct architectural styles.

landmarks.name: UC Davis Arboretum
landmarks.quote: To the south side of the campus core is the 100-acre UC Davis Arboretum, which includes 3.5 miles of paved paths, 4,000 tree specimens
landmarks.look: Expansive garden with paved paths and thousands of diverse trees.

landmarks.name: Lake Spafford
landmarks.quote: which includes 3.5 miles of paved paths, 4,000 tree specimens, Putah Creek and Lake Spafford.
landmarks.look: Calm lake within the arboretum surrounded by trees and paths.

landmarks.name: Mrak Hall
landmarks.quote: When Mrak retired in 1969, the campus administration building was named Mrak Hall in his honor.

landmarks.name: Wellman Hall
landmarks.quote: The northeast side of campus holds more of the core buildings that were built earlier in UC Davis's history, such as Wellman Hall
landmarks.look: Older core academic hall on the northeast side of campus.

landmarks.name: Manetti Shrem Museum of Art
landmarks.quote: Museums on campus include the C.N. Gorman Museum, specializing in indigenous and Native American art; and the Manetti Shrem Museum of Art
